quality_assessment: Excellent chapter with accurate documentation. Very minor improvements possible around implementation details and edge cases. All core sorting features are correctly documented with good examples and performance guidance.

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention the optimization for forward path sorting
issues.should_add: For ascending path sorting (--sort path without reverse), ripgrep uses an optimized path that avoids collecting all results into memory, processing paths in natural traversal order.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note that --sort path (ascending) is optimized and doesn't require buffering all results, unlike other sort modes including --sortr path
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:783 - special case for SortModeKind::Path if !sort.reverse

issues.description: Chapter states 'sorting disables parallelism' but doesn't explain the specific implementation detail
issues.current_content:
Sorting affects performance in several ways:

1. **Disables Parallelism**: Sorting requires collecting all results before output, so ripgrep runs single-threaded
issues.should_be: Sorting requires collecting all results before output. This automatically disables parallelism in the directory walker, forcing sequential processing. Exception: --sort path (ascending) uses an optimized streaming path.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add clarification that sorting disables parallelism at the directory walker level by collecting all haystacks before processing, and mention the optimization for forward path sorting

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention that path sorting with reverse is handled differently than forward
issues.current_content:
Reverse the sort order:

```bash
# Sort by path in reverse (descending)
rg --sortr path pattern
issues.should_add: Note that reverse path sorting (`--sortr path`) collects and sorts all paths in memory, unlike forward path sorting which can stream results.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a performance note that --sortr path has different memory characteristics than --sort path (the latter being optimized to avoid buffering when in ascending order)
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:783-789 - reverse path sorting uses .collect() and .reverse()

issues.description: Missing detail about timestamp error handling during sort
issues.current_content: Sort options section lists the various sort criteria
issues.should_add: When sorting by timestamps, files with metadata errors appear last in ascending order and first in descending order (with --sortr).
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a subsection on error handling that explains how files with inaccessible metadata are positioned in the sorted output
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/hiargs.rs:801-813 - timestamp sorting with None handling

issues.description: Performance comparison provides specific numbers that appear to be estimates rather than actual benchmarks
issues.current_content:
Example timing for large codebases (actual values depend on hardware, file count, and filesystem):
- Unsorted: ~100ms
- Sorted by path: ~500ms
- Sorted by time: ~600ms (requires stat calls)
issues.should_be: Keep the disclaimer clear that these are illustrative examples only
issues.fix_suggestion: The chapter already has good disclaimer text. This is actually well-handled. Consider this a non-issue.
